answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a public atlas of verifiable work history: every identity accumulates attestations from completed tasks, and trust decays over time so old history cannot be reused forever. New identities start at zero reputation and must earn access through small, rate-limited jobs before touching high-value work. Forging a credible history requires actually doing the work — like carving basalt, each attestation is slow and costly, so an attacker who tries to forge a thousand fake agents faces a thousand-fold work bill and still starts at zero trust.
